method: Same selection system as live play: random subjects and formats, then random unseen questions. Recent subjects are avoided to keep the mix varied; first 100.

questions.prompt: Name a city that has hosted the modern Olympics.
questions.scope: Summer and Winter hosts count; ancient host cities alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that has a protective shell, carapace, bony plates or body armour.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a game on Steam tagged “Battle Royale”.
Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.
questions.scope: Mouth-blown instruments count, including reed, brass and free-reed instruments.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Memphis Grizzlies.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Vancouver Grizzlies seasons also count.

questions.prompt: Name a building material.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a romance movie.
Name a spoken, signed or constructed language.
Name a pasta shape.
questions.scope: Named pasta shapes count; sauces and full dishes are separate.

questions.prompt: Name something that can be controlled with a remote.
questions.scope: A real consumer product type with a handheld or app-based remote qualifies.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of deer.
questions.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named animal groups, count. English names, documented scientific names and genuine public synonyms count. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with k-pop music.
Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
questions.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

questions.prompt: Name an item that can be used as furnace fuel in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Items actually accepted in the fuel slot count, rather than anything that merely looks flammable. Their fuel value need not be the same. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a real garden, botanical garden or arboretum.
questions.scope: Real named gardens, botanical gardens, arboretums and established garden complexes or garden estates count. Fictional gardens and an ordinary private address without a named garden do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a unit used to measure a physical quantity or digital information.
questions.scope: Established metric, customary, historical and scientific measurement units count, including named prefixed units. Currency units and arbitrary made-up units do not. Official unit symbols are accepted only when they name that actual unit.

questions.prompt: Name a type of footwear.
Name a dog breed, including historical breeds.
Name a named dish or preparation in which eggs are a main ingredient.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a guitar manufacturer or established guitar brand, including historical makers.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name an enchantment in Minecraft.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name a government-issued currency, monetary unit or named historical coin.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
questions.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

questions.prompt: Name an anime TV or streaming show.
Name an animal that can deliver venom.
questions.scope: Venom must be injected or delivered by a bite, sting or spine; simply being poisonous is different.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish cooked or wrapped in plant leaves.
questions.scope: Traditional leaf-wrapped food parcels, dishes cooked between leaves or in leaf-lined containers, and dishes traditionally sold wrapped in leaves count. Food merely set on a leaf plate without leaf cooking or wrapping does not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
questions.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

questions.prompt: Name a stadium, arena or racetrack used for professional sports.
questions.scope: Named venues anywhere in the world count; past venue names would be aliases.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Rihanna.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Rihanna count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer.

questions.prompt: Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
questions.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a character from the Harry Potter books or films.
questions.scope: Identifiable characters in the Harry Potter novels, films and their epilogues count, including creatures, ghosts and portraits. Real actors are not their fictional characters. Same-name characters share one answer identity.

questions.prompt: Name a type of building or place used for worship.
questions.scope: Types of religious worship building or built shrine count across religions. Individual named landmarks and a minister or deity alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that can produce its own light.
questions.scope: Bioluminescence, including light produced by symbiotic bacteria in an animal's light organ, counts. Reflection, fluorescence and bright coloring alone do not. Broad animal groups count when they contain documented luminous members.

questions.prompt: Name a tool, instrument or piece of glassware used in a science laboratory.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name someone who has played Major League Baseball (through 2025).
Name a food that is commonly pickled.
questions.scope: Vegetables, fruits, eggs, meats and seafood with established pickled preparations count. Vinegar and brine are ingredients, not foods being pickled.

questions.prompt: Name a record label or record company.
questions.scope: Real current and historical record labels, imprints and record companies count. A publisher, streaming platform or music store is not automatically a record label.

questions.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
questions.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

questions.prompt: Name a river, lake, sea, ocean, gulf, bay or strait.
Name a tool or piece of equipment used for gardening.
questions.scope: Tools, devices and durable equipment used to plant, water, prune, move soil or maintain gardens count. Plant names are not tools.

questions.prompt: Name a wild animal that spends time both in water and on land.
questions.scope: The animal must normally use both habitats, not merely survive a brief swim.

questions.prompt: Name an art or craft activity.
questions.scope: Established types and named examples count. Alternate standard names are the same answer.

questions.prompt: Name a water sport or recreational activity on or in water.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a seasoning, including herbs, spices and named spice blends.
Name a champion in League of Legends.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name an artist associated with pop music.
Name a piece of camping equipment.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a landlocked country.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of computer memory, storage device or storage medium.
questions.scope: Memory technologies and physical digital data-storage media or devices count, including obsolete systems. A song, movie or other recorded work is content, not storage. Online service brand names do not identify storage hardware.

questions.prompt: Name a type of ball used in a sport, game or athletic training.
questions.scope: Named balls used in sports, games or athletic training count, including particular game-ball designs. Pucks, shuttlecocks and punching bags are not balls.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of flatbread.
questions.scope: Recognized flatbread types, named regional breads and flatbread dishes count, including leavened and unleavened types. Ordinary sandwich loaves, toppings and ingredients alone do not count.

questions.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
questions.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of animal that can regrow a lost body part.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a musical artist or band with a number in their name.
questions.scope: Numbers written as digits, words or Roman numerals count.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of physical barrier.
questions.scope: Physical barriers such as walls, doors, fences, gates and protective barriers count. Figurative barriers and software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a desert.
questions.scope: Real named deserts and established desert regions worldwide count, including polar deserts and places traditionally known as deserts. A hotel, village, isolated rock, beach or generic dune does not automatically become a desert.

questions.prompt: Name a type of paint.
questions.scope: Types of paint defined by medium, finish or purpose count, including artist and building paints. Color names alone, a layer of paint and digital painting software do not.

questions.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
questions.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

questions.prompt: Name a named dish commonly made with chicken.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a named object in our Solar System.
questions.scope: Planets, dwarf planets, moons, named asteroids and named comets count; stars beyond the Sun do not.

questions.prompt: Name a playable hero in Dota 2.
questions.scope: The complete official playable hero roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts. Items, cosmetics and non-playable creeps are not heroes.

questions.prompt: Name a dinosaur or other prehistoric animal.
Name a type of boat, ship or other watercraft.
questions.scope: Kinds of boat, ship, raft or other vessel designed to travel on water or underwater count, past or present. Individual named vessels, wrecks, ice-only vehicles and descriptors of condition alone do not.

questions.prompt: Name a song by Linkin Park.
questions.scope: Released recordings credited to Linkin Park count, including collaborations, features and released covers. Writing or production credit alone does not count. Different versions share one answer. Released Xero and Hybrid Theory recordings from the same band also count; fan-contest songs do not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of exercise.
Name an exercise that can be done using your bodyweight instead of added weights.
questions.scope: Named exercises and recognized variations count, including floor exercises, holds and movements on a pull-up bar. A bar or bench can provide support; dumbbells and loaded barbells are not required.

questions.prompt: Name a food or drink made using fermentation.
questions.scope: Named foods, drinks and edible ingredients traditionally produced using microbial fermentation count, including foods subsequently cooked or distilled. An optional fermented ingredient does not make every mixed dish a separate fermentation product.

questions.prompt: Name a boss from Elden Ring.
questions.scope: The base game and Shadow of the Erdtree count; common short boss names would be aliases.

questions.prompt: Name a food crop with an edible part that normally grows underground.
questions.scope: Roots, tubers, rhizomes, bulbs, corms and underground fruits count. Named crop kinds and established edible varieties count. A normal above-ground fruit does not count merely because the plant has roots.

questions.prompt: Name a food named after a place.
questions.scope: The place name must appear in an established food or dish name.

questions.prompt: Name a real astronaut or cosmonaut.
questions.scope: Professional astronauts, cosmonauts and taikonauts worldwide, past or present, count, including people selected for professional astronaut training even if they never flew. Private-company professional astronauts and payload specialists count; celebrity passengers and fictional characters are not automatically astronauts.

questions.prompt: Name a style of coat or jacket.
questions.scope: Named coat and jacket styles count, including workwear and historical garments. Materials alone and coats of paint do not.

questions.prompt: Name a princess from fiction.
questions.scope: Characters who are, were, or are explicitly known as princesses count, along with the official Disney Princess lineup. A character does not qualify simply by being female, wearing a crown or appearing in a Disney movie.

questions.prompt: Name a dance style, traditional dance, or named social dance.
Name a game on Steam tagged “Strategy”.
Name an ice-cream topping or mix-in.
questions.scope: Named toppings and mix-ins used on ice cream, gelato or frozen custard count, including candy, fruit, nuts, sauces and cake pieces. A flavor by itself is not a topping.

questions.prompt: Name a landmark people can visit.
questions.scope: Named natural or human-made visitor landmarks count, including ruins.

questions.prompt: Name a sport or event that has appeared at the modern Olympics.
questions.scope: Summer and Winter Games count, including discontinued events.

questions.prompt: Name a structure or component found in a living cell.
questions.scope: Plant, animal, fungal and prokaryotic cell structures count. Whole organs or tissues are not structures inside one cell. Established molecular structures such as DNA and chromosomes count. Cellular structures and molecular assemblies count; an individual pigment such as chlorophyll is not an organelle or cell structure by itself.

questions.prompt: Name an object designed to be inflated.
questions.scope: Common inflatable objects and named inflatable equipment types count, whether filled with air, helium or another gas. Objects merely containing an empty cavity do not qualify.

questions.prompt: Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
questions.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

questions.prompt: Name an item that restores health in a video game.
questions.scope: Named consumables, pickups and healing items count; name the actual item.

questions.prompt: Name a kind of duck, goose or swan.
questions.scope: Established named groups and species in the Anatidae bird family count, including recently extinct species. Common and scientific names are accepted. Real synonyms share an identity; unrelated birds and objects named after birds do not count. Recognized domestic duck and goose breeds also count.

questions.prompt: Name a volcano or named volcanic complex. Dormant and extinct ones count.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a type of custard or a dessert made with custard.
questions.scope: Named custards and desserts made using custard or custard powder count. A cream-only filling does not qualify merely because it is called cream.

questions.prompt: Name an actor who appears in a Marvel Cinematic Universe movie.
questions.scope: Released MCU feature films count; voice and motion-capture performances count too.

questions.prompt: Name a player who has played for the Sacramento Kings.
questions.scope: At least one first-team NBA, BAA or ABA game for this franchise counts, past or present. Coaches, draft rights and preseason-only appearances do not. Rochester Royals, Cincinnati Royals, Kansas City-Omaha Kings and Kansas City Kings seasons also count.

questions.prompt: Name something people open using a key or a code.
questions.scope: Physical objects and devices count; the code can be a password or combination.

questions.prompt: Name an optical instrument used to aid vision or examine things.
questions.scope: Real instruments that use light to aid sight, magnify, project, examine or measure an optical image or spectrum count. Acoustic and mass-analysis instruments do not qualify merely because a source groups them near spectrometers.

questions.prompt: Name an agent in Valorant.
questions.scope: Base-game and recorded expansion names count. Versions of the same named object count once.

questions.prompt: Name an animal that is active at night.
questions.scope: Normally nocturnal or regularly night-active animals count; occasional unusual behavior does not.

questions.prompt: Name a type of musical instrument. Named instrument families count.
Name a named salad or established salad variety.
questions.scope: Types, named examples and established synonyms count. This is a finite source inventory.

questions.prompt: Name a real named beach.
questions.scope: Real named coastal, lake and river beaches count. A city name qualifies when it is also the established name of a beach. A whole country, waterbody or general tourist region alone does not name a beach.

questions.prompt: Name an occupation or recognized job title.
Name a human muscle or muscle group.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name someone who has played in the WNBA.
Name a bird that cannot normally fly, including extinct flightless birds.
questions.scope: Named examples and standard alternative names count. This is a finite curated inventory, not an exhaustive list of every real-world possibility.

questions.prompt: Name a Minecraft block you can strip, scrape or unwax by using an axe on it.
questions.scope: This asks for the right-click/use action. Merely chopping or breaking a block does not qualify. Both stripping wood and removing copper oxidation or wax count. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

questions.prompt: Name a horror movie.
